title: Homomorphism theorem for finite-type group schemes over a field
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $G,H$ be separated group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism] of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $f:G\to H$ be a $k$-group-scheme homomorphism. Its scheme-theoretic kernel $N=G\times_{H,f,e_H}\operatorname{Spec}k$ is a closed normal subgroup scheme of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup, def-pc-fibre-product]. There are a separated finite-type $k$-group scheme $I$ and homomorphisms $q:G\to I$ and $i:I\to H$ such that $f=i\circ q$, $i$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and $q$ is faithfully flat and finitely presented. Faithfully flat here means flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and surjective on underlying spaces; finitely presented means locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. The homomorphism $q$ has scheme-theoretic kernel $N$, and identifies $I$ with the fppf sheaf quotient $G/N$: the sheafification of $R\mapsto G(R)/N(R)$ on commutative $k$-algebras for jointly surjective faithfully flat finitely presented coverings.

source.place: Theorem 5.39 (Homomorphism Theorem), printed p.108, with Theorem 5.28 and its following paragraph, printed p.105; Corollary 5.27 (torsor), printed p.105, and Section 5(j), Example 5.71, printed p.117, for the quotient-sheaf interpretation. Finite presentation follows since the group schemes are of finite type over a field.

proof.text: By [lem-sc-kernel-subgroup], $N$ is a closed subgroup scheme and $N(R)=\ker f(R)$. It is normal: for $g\in G(R)$ and $n\in N(R)$, $f(gng^{-1})=f(g)1f(g)^{-1}=1$; the inverse conjugation gives equality. It is of finite type: its closed underlying subset in the quasi-compact $G$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-in-quasi-compact]. On an affine finite-type chart $\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $G$, its inverse image is $\operatorname{Spec}(A/J)$ by [def-weil-closed-immersion]; the images of any finite set of $k$-algebra generators of $A$ generate $A/J$. A finite affine cover of $G$ therefore gives a finite affine finite-type cover of $N$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism].

source.place: Theorem 5.39, first sentence; normality of a kernel preceding Theorem 5.14, printed p.102; finite type from affine quotients.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-algebraic-group-homogeneous-quotient] to the closed subgroup $N\subset G$. Obtain a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $I$ and a flat surjective finitely presented map $q:G\to I$. For every test scheme $T$, two $G(T)$-points have the same $q$-image precisely when they differ by right multiplication by an $N(T)$-point. Every $I(T)$-point lifts on an fpqc covering. These statements apply without assuming that $N$ is smooth or that $G$ is affine.

source.place: Theorem 5.28, following paragraph and Proposition 5.25, printed p.105.

proof.text: Give $I(T)$ a group law by fpqc descent. Lift $x,y\in I(T)$ to $a,b$ locally and define $xy$ locally by $q(ab)$, $x^{-1}$ by $q(a^{-1})$, and $1$ by $q(1)$. For two choices, $a'=an$, $b'=bm$ with $n,m\in N$; then $a'b'=ab(b^{-1}nb)m$ and $b^{-1}nb\in N$ by normality. Also $(an)^{-1}=a^{-1}(an^{-1}a^{-1})$ with the last factor in $N$. Thus the coset criterion in [lem-sfb-algebraic-group-homogeneous-quotient] makes these values agree on overlaps. Base-change the covers using [lem-galois-fpqc-covering-base-change]; for two or three variables apply [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] successively over each cover, which both glues the values and detects their equality. The constructions are natural in $T$. Yoneda [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful], applied to schemes over $k$, turns them into morphisms $I\times_k I\to I$, $I\to I$, $\operatorname{Spec}k\to I$. Associativity, both unit laws and both inverse laws hold after lifting the variables, since they hold in $G$, and hence globally by uniqueness of descent. Therefore $I$ is a group scheme and $q$ is a homomorphism.

source.place: Paragraph after Theorem 5.28, printed p.105, and Proposition 5.12, printed p.101; descent as in Stacks Tag 023Q, descent-lemma-fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms; Yoneda Tag 001P, categories-lemma-yoneda; fpqc base change Tag 022D, topologies-lemma-fpqc (3).

proof.text: For $x\in I(T)$ choose an fpqc-local lift $a\in G$. Set $i(x)=f(a)$ locally. If $a'=an$ with $n\in N$, then $f(a')=f(a)$, so [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] for $H$ glues these values uniquely. The result is natural in $T$ and thus gives a morphism $i:I\to H$ by [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful]. The formula gives $iq=f$; applying it to products gives $i(xy)=i(x)i(y)$ locally and hence globally by descent. Thus $i$ is a homomorphism. It is injective on every test scheme's points: if $i(x)=i(y)$, lift $x,y$ on covers and compare on their fibre products [lem-galois-fpqc-covering-base-change]. There $f(a)=f(b)$, so $a^{-1}b\in N$, whence $q(a)=q(b)$ by the quotient's coset criterion. Uniqueness of descent for $I$ gives $x=y$.

source.place: Theorem 5.13 and its proof, printed p.101, used in Theorem 5.39, printed p.108; injectivity is the explicit coset argument; Stacks Tags 023Q, 022D and 001P as in step 3.

proof.text: The hypotheses of [lem-sfb-algebraic-group-monomorphism-closed-immersion] hold for $i$: both $I$ and $H$ are separated and of finite type over $k$, and step 4 proves injectivity on all commutative $k$-algebras. Hence $i$ is a closed immersion. For every $T$, $q(a)=1$ if and only if $a^{-1}\in N(T)$ by the coset criterion, equivalently $a\in N(T)$. Thus $N$ is the scheme-theoretic kernel of $q$, by the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] and Yoneda [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful].

source.place: Theorem 5.39, last sentence, printed p.108; Theorem 5.34, printed p.107; kernel from the coset criterion in Definition 5.20.

proof.text: Finally restrict to affine tests $\operatorname{Spec}R$. The maps $G(R)/N(R)\to I(R)$ are injective by the coset criterion. They are fppf-locally surjective: base-change the fppf covering $q:G\to I$ along any $x:\operatorname{Spec}R\to I$ using [lem-trf-fppf-covering-base-change], and take its finite affine refinement [lem-pc-fppf-affine-refinement]; the projection to $G$ is the required lift. The representable $I$ is a sheaf by [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent]. For any sheaf $F$ and natural map $G(-)/N(-)\to F$, evaluate locally on such coset lifts. Two lifts agree as cosets on their overlap because their images in $I$ agree; hence their $F$-values agree and glue uniquely. Refining two choices proves independence, and uniqueness of gluing gives naturality. This is exactly the universal property of sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], so $I$ represents the stated fppf quotient. Flatness, surjectivity and finite presentation of $q$ were supplied in step 2.

source.place: Example 5.71, printed p.117, and Corollary 5.27, printed p.105; fppf rather than only fpqc lifts via Stacks Tags 021O (topologies-lemma-fppf) and 021P (topologies-lemma-fppf-affine).
